articles.title: Will Bad Weather Disrupt Thanksgiving Travel?
articles.summary: Millions are expected to travel this week ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, but stormy weather and coastal flooding in parts of the country could disrupt plans during one of the year’s busiest travel periods. AAA projects 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home for Thanksgiving between Tuesday, Nov. 24 and Monday, Nov. 30. articles.title: 6 Questions About Jensen Huang's Stunning Return as Nvidia CEO
articles.summary: Eleven days. That’s how long it took Jensen Huang to return to his post of CEO of Nvidia after resigning in the wake of an alleged espionage scandal that rocked the business, tech, and policy worlds. On Nov. 12, Huang stepped down from the company he co-founded in 1993 after acknowledging an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese national whom U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspected was a Chinese spy. articles.title: The Failed U.N. COP31 Deal Reveals a New Reality for Climate Action
articles.summary: In the eleven years since the Paris Agreement , countries around the world have met annually to plot out the global consensus on how to tackle climate change. In some years negotiations led to big breakthroughs. In others, talks simply kept the ball in play, signaling to the world that nations were aligned in their desire to tackle climate change, even if it’s hard to agree on the exact path forward. articles.title: How Taiwan Is Turning Tech Supremacy Into a Security Shield
articles.summary: The southern Taiwanese city of Chiayi has long been synonymous with a cherished culinary staple: turkey rice, served drenched in savory soy broth and topped with lard-fried shallots and pickled radish. Introduced by American GIs after World War II, the non-native bird became an affordable alternative to chicken and quickly became a local icon. articles.title: Why the Ebola Outbreak Keeps Growing, According to Virus Expert Pardis Sabeti
articles.summary: The ongoing Ebola outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is now the second largest on record.
